correctness.rationale: Reduction acts on the projective dual via invertible generators, and the finite orbit is the image of the complex orbit under reduction at the specified prime. The independent reconstruction gave 45 distinct reduced lines. Every reduced pair-intersection is the specialization of its generic pair-intersection, so the classical and reduced censuses both being 201 give a bijection preserving all incidences. Ordinary points blow up to distinct transverse branches on exceptional rational components. This gives 246 rational components and 720 nodes in a connected graph with minimum degree three, hence stability and arithmetic genus 475. Exact recomputation verifies the joint eigenblocks by the annihilating polynomial, traces, and projectors. The Schur numerator uses all three point degrees on 27 line eigendirections and degrees 3 and 4 on the other 18, leaving (t−3)^75 and (t−5)^9 as the pure factors; the checked numerators give the claimed characteristic polynomial with simple zero. The matrix-tree formula yields the stated order. Local Smith reduction uses unit row/column operations with minimum valuation pivots, so over Z/p^h each pivot's residue valuation gives the exponent when less than h. Four distinct rooted cofactors yielded the same positive valuations at all six primes. The valuation totals match the independently reproduced tree order, so no other primes can occur; aligning the valuations gives all 76 nonunit factors and the stated exponent. For a regular unit-thickness semistable model the component intersection matrix is the negative graph Laplacian, and the usual degree-zero quotient gives the stated conditional Jacobian Néron component group.
residual_risks: The complex arrangement is identified by the incidence-preserving reduction argument, not a separate coordinate computation over C. No smoothing existence or model with nonunit thickness is claimed.
